chunks: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, the One, the Unique, who has no partner; the Peerless, the Self-Sufficient, who has no equal; the First, the Eternal, who has no limit; the Last, the Everlasting, who has no end; the Existing, the Constant, who has no non-existence; the Eternal King, who does not decline; the All-Powerful, whom nothing weakens; the All-Knowing, from whom nothing is hidden; the Living, not by acquired life; the Existing, not confined to a place; the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing, who has no instrument or tool; the One who commanded justice, accepted bounty, and decreed finality; none can reverse His decree, nor counter His judgment, nor overpower His will. And His command, when He intends anything, is only to say to it, 'Be,' and it is. So exalted is He in whose Hand is the dominion of all things, and to Him is the return and the final destination.

And I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, Lord of the worlds; and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, Master of the Prophets and the best of all His creation; and I bear witness that Ali ibn Abi Talib is the Master of the Appointed Guardians, Imam of the Pious, and Commander of the Radiant-foreheaded; and that the Imams from his progeny after him are the Proofs of Allah until the Day of Judgment; may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all.

The Shaykh, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi, the jurist, resident of Ray, compiler of this book (may Allah assist him in obeying Him and grant him success in pleasing Him), said: What prompted me to compile this book is that I found a group of our opponents who attribute to us the belief in anthropomorphism (tashbih) and determinism (jabr), because they found in their books traditions (akhbar) which they did not know how to interpret, nor understand their meanings, and placed them in the wrong context, and did not compare their wording with the wording of the Quran. As a result, they distorted the image of our sect in the eyes of the ignorant, confused people regarding our path, turned people away from the religion of Allah, and induced them to deny the Proofs of Allah. Therefore, I sought closeness to Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, by compiling this book on Divine Unity (Tawhid), refuting anthropomorphism and determinism, relying on Him and placing my trust in Him, and He is sufficient for me and the best Disposer of affairs.

key_terms.الْغُرِّ الْمُحَجَّلِينَ: The Radiant-foreheaded (a title for the Prophet and Imams)
key_terms.حُجَجُ اللَّهِ: Proofs of Allah (referring to the Imams)

ai.seo_question: Why did Ibn Babawayh write the book Al-Tawhid?
ai.summary: Authored by Shaykh al-Saduq (Ibn Babawayh) in the 10th century, this foreword establishes the theological foundation of 'Al-Tawhid' by addressing the specific doctrinal disputes of his era, particularly the accusations of anthropomorphism (tashbih) and determinism (jabr) leveled against the Shia by opponents like the Mu'tazila and others. The text highlights the scholarly method of reconciling hadith with the Quran to preserve the purity of the Shia creed, emphasizing the Imams as the enduring proofs (hujaj) of God. This work remains a cornerstone of Shia kalām for its systematic refutation of these key theological deviations.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: All praise be to Allah, the One and Only, who does not have a partner; the Peerless, the Needless, who has no like; the First, the Ever-Existent, who has no limit; the Last and the Everlasting who has no end; the Existing, the Constant, who has no non-existence; the Eternal King, who does not decline; the Power who is not weakened; the All-Knowing from who nothing can be hidden; the Alive but not with life; the One who Exists, but who is not confined to place; the All-Hearing and the All-Seeing, who has no ears and eyes; the One who ordered with justice, punished with favour, and commanded with bounty, but not to trap people under His Command. There is no rejecter to His Judgement, no challenger to His Decision, and no subduer to His Will. And His Command, when He intendeth anything, is only that He sayeth unto it “Be,” and then it is. Therefore, hallowed be He in whose Hand is the kingdom of all things, and unto His is the return and final arrival.

And I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, the Master of the Universe, and I bear witness that Muhammad (sw) in His Servant and His Messenger, the Master of the Prophets (of Allah) and the Best of all His Creation. And I bear witness that `Ali ibn Abu Talib (AS) is the Master of the Appointed Guardians, and Commander of the Pious and Leader of the People with Radiant Foreheads. And I bear witness that the Imams (AS) from his Progeny after him are the Proofs of Allah to the Day of Judgement; may the blessings and salutations of Allah be upon them all.

Al-Shaykh Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn `Ali ibn Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi, the jurist, a resident of Ray compiler of this book (may Allah, the Exalted, help him in obeying Him, and grant him success with his work, through His Contentment) said: I compiled this book because the opponents of our sect [isabah] allege that we believe in anthropomorphism and determinism [jabr]. They made these claims on the basis of traditions [akhbar] they found in their books. Since they could not explain these traditions, and they could not understand their meaning, they distorted their original sense. In fact, they failed to compare the words of these traditions with the words of the Quran. As a result of their shortcomings, they distorted the beliefs of our sects among the ignorant. They confused people about our ways, and turned people away from the religion of Allah. They induced them to deny the Proofs of Allah. Therefore, I sought the favour of Allah, may His Remembrance be Exalted, and sought His Help, through the compilation of The Book of Divine Unity which rejects anthropomorphism and determinism.
